seoTitle: How to Loop Audio in Canva Without Gaps
metaDescription: Loop background music or sound effects in Canva by duplicating and aligning audio tracks on your project timeline for continuous playback.
intro: Background music that cuts out partway through a presentation or video can feel jarring, but Canva doesn't have a one-click loop button for audio. This guide covers duplicating and aligning your audio track manually so it plays continuously across your entire project, with smooth fades to hide the seams.

steps.heading: Upload or select your audio
steps.body: Choose a track from the Canva audio library or upload your own file, then add it to your project timeline.

steps.heading: Select the audio layer
steps.body: Click the audio track on the timeline to open its adjustment options.

steps.heading: Duplicate and extend the track
steps.body: Duplicate the audio section and extend it across multiple pages to cover the full length of your project.

steps.heading: Align start and end points
steps.body: Line up the start and end points of each duplicated section so the audio loops continuously without gaps.

steps.heading: Add fade transitions
steps.body: Apply fade in and fade out effects to smooth over the transitions between looped sections.

steps.heading: Adjust volume and preview
steps.body: Balance the background track volume against any voiceover, then preview the full playback to confirm the loop sounds seamless.

faq.question: Does Canva have a built-in loop button for audio?
faq.answer: No, Canva doesn't offer a single-click loop feature, so looping requires manually duplicating and aligning the audio track across your timeline.

faq.question: Why does my looped audio have a noticeable gap or click?
faq.answer: This usually happens when the start and end points of duplicated sections aren't precisely aligned — adding fade transitions can also help mask small gaps.

faq.question: Can I loop audio behind a voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes, you can adjust the background track's volume level separately so it plays continuously without overpowering your narration.

faq.question: Does this work for both presentations and videos?
faq.answer: Yes, the same timeline-based looping approach applies whether you're working on a Canva presentation or a video project.
